claims.text: The driver's own GPS trace measures 19.71 km between the recorded pickup event and the recorded drop-off event, against a booked optimal route of 14.6 km. That is an excess of 5.11 km and 35.00% of optimal, so both limbs of the POL-RD-01 establishment test are satisfied: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The route deviation the rider complains of is established on this trip's own trace.

POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure the governing measurement and forbids citing the rounded trip-record copy for the threshold test. Here there is no conflict to resolve: the trace records 19.71 km and the trip record records 19.7 km, and the two agree to within rounding. The excess therefore stands uncorrected on either figure.

The trace is clean for policy purposes. It is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, carries 155 fixes at a 10-second sample interval with 100.0% coverage and no gaps, and its maximum gap is 0.0 seconds. POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is therefore not engaged, no independent corroboration is required and no ESCALATE is triggered under POL-RD-10(3).

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: fare_model reads UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is 21.50, so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess is. The rider's remedy is the POL-RD-11 route: the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote, plus any properly chargeable pass-through lines. The establishment finding above is relevant to the record, but the money follows the upfront arithmetic, not a recomputed metered fare.

The POL-RD-11(a) arithmetic is fixed on this fare. charged_total is SGD 31.80, quoted_fare is SGD 21.50 and the properly chargeable pass-through and statutory lines total SGD 0.00, giving 31.80 less 21.50 less 0.00 = SGD 10.30, which the fare ledger publishes as pol_rd_11_remedy. That is the sum the rider is owed.

To be accurate about the quantum: the rider contested SGD 14.00, but the policy measures the remedy on an upfront-quoted trip as the excess over the quote, which on this fare is SGD 10.30. I do not contend for the balance of the contested figure, because POL-RD-11(a) does not provide for it.

Nothing offsets that SGD 10.30. The fare carries zero ERP gantry lines (tolls_erp 0.00), no airport surcharge (0.00), and a waiting_time_fee of 0.00, so the properly chargeable pass-through total under POL-RD-09 is 0.00 and no statutory line reduces the refund. There is likewise no off-route or phantom gantry line to correct under POL-RD-09(4), and none is claimed.

No rider-requested detour can be invoked against this claim. The chat log for this trip carries 0 messages, so there is no rider instruction that could meet POL-RD-04(a) to (c), no waypoint_hint to corroborate and no distance to exclude from the excess on that ground.

No endpoint amendment relieves the driver either. The trip record shows amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null and pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and no amended optimal route displaces the booked 14.6 km baseline.

This is not a pooled trip, so POL-RD-12 does not re-base the comparison. The trip record gives vehicle_type RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null; the baseline is therefore the single optimal route of 14.6 km recorded at booking, and the co-rider exclusion has no application.

I disclose that the traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02814-01 is MISSING: it carries no payload, has admissibility status MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0, and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT. I cite it for the absence itself. Because no advisory covers this trip window, POL-RD-03 cannot be run, and no external traffic cause can be established on this record. The trace's own derived advisory block returns an empty advisory list against POL-RD-03, consistent with the missing artifact.

The driver's counterparty statement — 'The meter adds the extra distance' — names no evidence ID and invokes no clause. POL-RD-08 provides that an assertion which cites no evidence ID is discarded, and that once the rider has shown a matching trip and a threshold excess the driver must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause. This assertion points to neither, and on an upfront-quoted trip the 'meter' explanation is beside the point in any event, because the distance lines were fixed at booking.

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all describe the same trip TRP-02814, the pickup event at 11:57:30 on 2026-08-10 is common to trace and trip record, and the excess of 5.11 km / 35.00% meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden has shifted to the driver and has not been discharged.

The rider profile adds no corroboration requirement to this claim. POL-RD-08's extra-corroboration factor applies only where deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer; here deviation_claims_60d is 1. In any event the excess is 35.00%, above the 30% figure that factor speaks to, so the trace alone carries the finding.

The payment state matters to the ruling value. The fare ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the rider is presently carrying the disputed over-charge. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative and would leave that charge exactly where it is; only a refund under POL-RD-11(a) moves the SGD 10.30 back to the rider.

The fare model on this trip is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is 21.50, both read straight off the fare breakdown, so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run. The rider's distance and time charges were fixed at booking; the measured 5.11 km / 35.00% route excess therefore generates no distance-or-time refund however much longer the driven route looks beside the quote.

Under POL-RD-11(a) the only refundable sum is charged_total (31.80) less quoted_fare_sgd (21.50) less the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. Every such line on this ledger is zero - erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp 0.00, airport_surcharge 0.00 and waiting_time_fee 0.00 - so properly_chargeable totals 0.00 and the remedy is 10.30, not the 14.00 the rider contests.

The excess on the governing trace figure is 5.11 km, or 35.00% of the 14.6 km optimal route. POL-RD-01's establishment tests pass, but neither materiality limb does: 35.00% is below the 50% mark and 5.11 km is below the 8.0 km mark. This is therefore not a MATERIAL deviation, POL-RD-06's driver-profile check is not engaged, and neither the FULL_REFUND uplift at limb (b) nor the driver-conduct referral at limb (c) is available against this driver.

Even if POL-RD-06 were consulted, the only two profile fields that clause permits decide it for the driver: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 396. Zero flags fails the 3-flag limb, and 0/396 fails the 0.05 ratio limb (which additionally requires at least 40 completed trips), so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no uplift or referral can be built on the driver's record.

Nothing may be stacked on top of that figure. POL-RD-11(b) is not added to POL-RD-11(a), and the ledger carries no off-route or phantom line for POL-RD-09(4) to correct: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.00 and airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. The rider's recovery is the capped arithmetic and nothing besides.

The driver's answer - 'the meter adds the extra distance' - describes what the ledger already shows (a 31.80 charge against a 21.50 quote); it is not a clause-anchored excuse, and no exculpatory route is open on this record. The chat log holds 0 messages so POL-RD-04 cannot run; pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null so POL-RD-05 cannot run; and vehicle_type is RYDE_X so POL-RD-12 cannot run. The driver's position is accordingly that the rider recovers the capped upfront-quote figure and no more.
